findings.reason: two concurrent workers on `reckon/serve.py` is the collision the plan's own ordering sentences exist to prevent, and the edge is one entry in the declarations.
findings.text: §12 is declared implementable and edits `reckon/serve.py`, but the plan's scheduling edge for it is absent: `plan-section-depends-on` lists only `s11` and `s7`, and §12's prose omits the "runs after … which shares `reckon/serve.py`" sentence that §3, §6, §7 and §11 each carry, so the scheduler can dispatch §11 and §12 in the same wave against one file.

findings.reason: without a case for the bound check the node can close on a half-fix, and the section already argues the rotation is part of the harm.
findings.text: §12's deliverable asserts two consumers share the bound path ("Every access line and bound check of that server uses that path") and names one control that reverts the per-line resolution of the access line only, so an implementation that binds the line path while `_bound_server_log` (reckon/serve.py:285,297) keeps resolving per call passes the gate with the rotation harm §12's own Why names still live.

findings.reason: the binding site is the whole mechanism, and the plan's own done-when test only passes if it is attached somewhere every server object passes through, which the plan does not say.
findings.text: the deliverable says a served process "resolves its log path once, when the server starts serving" and names no construction the binding attaches to, while the defect it measured was produced by a `serve.Handler` under a bare `ThreadingHTTPServer` a test builds itself (`tests/test_cross_node_writes_refresh_the_index.py:206`), which never passes through the served entry point (`reckon/serve.py:4064`) where the only existing `_bound_server_log()` call sits (reckon/serve.py:4084); a worker taking the natural reading — bind in the entry point — gets a test that cannot reach the binding and a fix that leaves every test-built server leaking.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `tests/test_cross_node_writes_refresh_the_index.py::test_an_open_stream_receives_the_added_row_and_stays_open` resolves at line 398 of that file, and `Handler.log_message` (reckon/serve.py:2230), `_write_access_line` (255/263), `_server_log_path` (255), `_bound_server_log` (285) and `_config_home` (reckon/_store.py:128) all resolve, with `_server_log_path` → `reckon.service.log_path` → `_config_home()/logs/server.log` producing the cited `~/.config/reckon/logs/server.log`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §12's one case falsifies only the access-line half of its deliverable; the deliverable's second clause ("Every access line and bound check of that server uses that path") has no case, so a fix to the line path alone passes the gate while a test process still rotates the operator's log.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §12 puts every log under the run directory with a revision header and a bare `EXIT=` line, the durable convention §10 and §11 use; the measured probe's counts are stated inline (85 `/_changes/sample` lines in the live log at review time, matching the plan's "after" figure).
rubric_items.naming: pass — §12 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket or version into the two names it touches, and its prose describes the mechanism (a path resolved once per served process) rather than a tracker entry.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable binds the path "when the server starts serving" but names no construction it attaches to, while the harm §12 measured is produced by a server the served entry point never constructs, so the fix as specified can leave the measured case in place.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §12 carries one deliverable (one resolution point for the served log path) plus the coordinator's confirmation of the same mechanism, the shape §10 and §11 already use.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §12 writes `reckon/serve.py` and declares no ordering edge to §11, which is declared implementable and writes the same file; `plan-section-depends-on` (docs/plans/the-page-paints-from-an-index.html:29) carries only `s11` and `s7`.
